title: Ephemeral scrub and staged deletion gateway for analytics events
creator: Priya Desai
description: Build an intermediary gateway in the console analytics ingestion path that performs timebound ‘ephemeral scrubbing’ for sensitive fields and stages records into a tombstone lifecycle for safe deletion. Goals: (1) minimize latency impact for real-time dashboards, (2) ensure scrubbed events are reversible for a short legal hold window only when authorized, (3) provide auditable deletion attestations and material suitable for compliance export. This ticket covers the backend gateway, associated metadata schema changes, and orchestration hooks to the deletion/retention coordinator. It does NOT include the UI workflow for manual erasure requests (separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts incoming event batches and applies configured scrub rules with <100ms median added latency for 95th percentile payloads
Scrubbed values are replaced with ephemeral tokens and stored alongside a minimal reversible vault reference that expires after the configured hold window
Events marked for staged deletion enter the tombstone queue and are removed from downstream analytic sinks after tombstone expiry
Audit log entries are emitted for every scrub and deletion action with trace IDs and operator identity
E2E tests cover: scrub rule application, tombstone lifecycle progression, and blocked deletion under active legal hold
implementation_notes: Design decision: use a short-lived reversible vault (KMS-wrapped key per-customer) for authorized rehydration instead of long-term PII storage
We will implement scrub rules as a layered pipeline: deterministic field rules (emails, credit-card-like tokens) -> regex heuristics -> ML-based sensitive-detector fallback
Prefer single-process fast-path in the gateway for common events; fallback async worker for heavy ML checks to avoid tail latency
Metrics: instrument scrub_rate, scrub_latency_p50/p95, tombstone_enqueue_rate, tombstone_expiry_rate, rehydrate_requests
Failure mode: on gateway error, default to safe-skip (drop sensitive fields) and emit incident metric; team agreed to metric-led rollback rather than blocking ingestion
